draft.title: Movement terms
card: Flexion and extension
Flexion decreases the angle at a joint, such as bending the elbow. Extension increases the angle, such as straightening the elbow.
Abduction and adduction
Abduction moves a limb away from the midline of the body, such as lifting an arm out to the side. Adduction moves it back towards the midline.
Rotation
Rotation turns a body part around its own long axis, such as turning the head to look over a shoulder.
Circumduction
Circumduction swings a limb in a circle, so the end of the limb traces a cone shape. A bowler's arm in a cricket overarm action is an example.
draft.remember: Match the movement to what happens: angle changes, towards or away from the midline, a turn, or a circle.

a.q: Priya stands with her arms by her sides and lifts both arms out to the side. What is this movement at the shoulder?
a.why: The arms move away from the midline of the body, which is abduction. Adduction is tempting, but it describes the return movement towards the midline.
a.clue: Are the arms moving away from the middle of the body or towards it?

b.q: Liam is at the bottom of a squat and stands up, so his knees go from bent to straight. What is the movement at the knee?
b.why: Standing up straightens the knee and increases the angle at the joint, which is extension. Flexion is tempting because the squat bends the knee, but flexion decreases the angle and describes the way down.
b.clue: Does the angle at the knee get bigger or smaller as he stands?

problems.detail: The circumduction line says 'the end of the limb traces a cone shape'. It is the whole limb that sweeps out a cone; the end of the limb traces a circle. Suggest: 'Circumduction swings a limb in a circle, so the limb traces a cone shape.'
